assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the building of a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice opened a new window on the universe. It is an instrument-driven discovery with a clear, original concept and lasting impact on multimessenger astrophysics. As an experimentalist in astroparticle detection I regard this as a very strong case.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept and its funding; Spiering led the European and German contributions and the earlier AMANDA and Baikal-era detector development. The supplied credit names two people, which fits a prize, though other leading figures (for example in AMANDA or the collaboration spokesperson roles) are not on the list and the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 diffuse-flux discovery has been confirmed by independent analyses and by the 2017 blazar coincidence and the 2023 Galactic-plane evidence. Interpretation of individual source classes is still evolving, but the central discovery is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Individual source identification remains only partly established.
Credit among AMANDA and IceCube founders beyond the two supplied names is uncertain, as I recall it.
I have a field-adjacent background, so I weigh claims on instrumentation carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification, followed by its experimental realization, founded the field of topological insulators. The originality and long-term impact across condensed matter, materials and spintronics are very large.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical advance; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not among the credited names). The three credited names give a coherent configuration, but the theory credit for HgTe is shared with others outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Many independent experiments in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and three-dimensional materials confirm the physics, and the 2016 prize on topological phases has paved the way. Recognition is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and others who are not in the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 prize themes may be weighed by the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. It is a clear, original, and high-impact discovery with a vast follow-up literature.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction of 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discoveries. The three credited names map naturally onto theory plus experiment, though other groups (such as Dean and Yacoby on related platforms) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups and platforms within a few years, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and several correlated states are still debated. Timely, though slightly early for a final interpretation.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate the reproducibility of some phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and pushed to 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, is a landmark in precision measurement with applications in tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the early clocks; Ye's group brought the precision and stability to the 10^-18 level, with a strontium clock and frequency-comb links. A two-person configuration is clean, though trapped-ion clock contributors are excluded by definition of the candidate.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance and the technology is advancing rapidly, so recognition would be timely. The frequency-comb part has already been awarded in 2005.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier prize for optical frequency-comb techniques and the competing ion-clock lineage.
Whether the redefinition of the second has to occur before recognition is for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed states for quantum-enhanced interferometry were proposed by Caves and then demonstrated in the laboratory and in gravitational-wave detectors, and they improve the sensitivity of instruments that were themselves recognised in 2017. It is conceptually clear and experimentally impactful.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the theory in 1981; Kimble's group, with Slusher's at Bell Labs (Slusher is not in the supplied names), produced the first squeezed light; Schnabel's team demonstrated detector-compatible squeezing at GEO600; Mavalvala is on the list but I do not rank her among my three. Credit is complex and no unique three-person solution exists.
assessment.maturity: Squeezed light is now in routine operation in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600, which is strong confirmation. The attribution makes timing difficult.
uncertainties: Missing key experimentalists in the credited names, in particular Slusher and Wu.
Whether the committee sees this as an enabling technique rather than a stand-alone discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The conception and construction of the LHC and of the general-purpose ATLAS and CMS detectors made the Higgs discovery and a decade of precision measurements possible. It is a monumental technical achievement, directly in the tradition of instrumentation that I know well.
assessment.attribution: Evans led the machine's construction; Della Negra and Jenni were founding leaders of CMS and ATLAS. The configuration is plausible, but the work was carried out by thousands, and others such as Gianotti and Virdee have strong claims on the detector side.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is confirmed and the performance is well established. The 2013 prize was for the theory of the mechanism, so experimental recognition is conceivable, but this is an instrumentation and big-collaboration case that the statutes handle awkwardly.
uncertainties: Whether a facility-and-detector prize fits the prize criteria.
Competing credit with the B055 discovery-focused candidacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of how CMB photons interact with hot cluster plasma (the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects) and of acoustic features in the primordial plasma gave cosmology two foundational tools, now used in cluster surveys and CMB analysis.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical contributions are strongly attributed to Sunyaev, with Zel'dovich deceased. A single-laureate configuration is simple, although the work was a collaboration in its original form and other contributors to the acoustic-oscillation theory (such as Peebles and Yu) are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: The SZ effect has been confirmed by several dedicated experiments (ACT, SPT, Planck) and is a standard cosmological probe. The recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Shared early credit with Zel'dovich, who cannot be recognised posthumously.
Overlap with the 2019 and 2006 cosmology prizes could affect how the committee views novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are a direct visual confirmation of black-hole shadows and a technical triumph in VLBI. The impact on strong-field gravity tests and astrophysics is high.
assessment.attribution: Falcke provided the shadow-imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT collaboration and the technical development, and Moran contributed the foundational mm-VLBI work. The collaboration is extremely large, so a three-person selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: The 2019 and 2022 results have been confirmed with polarization and multi-epoch data, though the interpretation of detailed morphology still depends on modelling. The recognition is possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Dependence on image-reconstruction and model assumptions.
Allocation of credit within an extremely large collaboration.
